the modeling and analysis of a prioritized optical switch architecture with FDLs.
the design and performance evaluation of an optical burst switch architecture that utilizes fiber delay lines as optical buffers.
modeling and analyzing the performance of optical burst switching networks.

the use of optical buffers can significantly enhance the performance of optical burst switching networks.

we have developed a general performance model for optical burst switches employing FDLs.

the use of FDLs as optical buffers can reduce the burst loss probabilities by an order of magnitude, while at the same time reducing the delay experienced by the low priority class by a factor of three or more.

the use of FDLs as optical buffers can significantly reduce the burst loss probabilities and the burst delay in a prioritized optical network.
the performance of optical burst switching can be significantly improved by employing FDLs as optical buffers, especially when burst lengths are long.
the performance of a prioritized optical switch with FDLs can be captured accurately using a simple model.
